accelerator.kernel_launch_overhead_cycle.source: Reference measurement from the existing compiler: vector parameter dispatch, instruction issue and pipeline fill/drain per pass on Sphinx. Reused without a separate measurement for this build.

accelerator.spmm_row_cycles.source: Reference measurement from the existing compiler: sparse accumulator turnaround per row on Sphinx, rounded to eight cycles. Used when the sparse path is enabled; not separately characterized for this build.

soc.bank_switch_cycles.source: Scratchpad read round-trip delay used when a request stream switches banks.

accelerator.cim.accumulation_feedback_cy.source: The delay before an accumulation write can safely be read again is not characterized.

accelerator.cim.output_bank_drain_cycles.source: Measured minimum control delay between draining an output tile and returning its accumulation bank. Other waiting is calculated separately.

accelerator.cim.output_pipeline.source: The streaming output route has not been separately characterized. Measured banked output uses banked_pipeline.

accelerator.cim.banked_pipeline.source: Synthesized accumulation-bank handoff and matrix-to-vector handshakes. The producer handoff is paid per completed bank tile. Forwarding is the additional delay beyond architectural result latency and that handoff. Vector stage capacities come from saturated valid/ready handshakes; minimum transit gives the forward delays. These describe retained data after bank release; the active serialized output vector is counted separately in code. Read-ahead beats are operand responses the input and weight controllers accept at their response handshakes before the destination buffer slot frees; requests held in system or test-harness response queues are excluded.

metadata.scope: The bank-drain measurement covers 64×64 INT8/INT24 CIM builds with two accumulation banks, two or eighteen resident weight sets, five local accumulation contexts and performance counters enabled. Sparse, matrix-vector and depthwise units are disabled. Banked scheduling covers direct INT24 stores and fused BF16 output without fetched operands; other routes retain architectural bounds.
metadata.hardware_source: CIM output path with address-first stores, early accumulation writes and five local accumulation contexts.
